title: The least functional dependence at negative footrule: the lower boundary of the region of Chatterjee's rank correlation and Spearman's footrule
description:
Unrefereed research candidate. Chatterjee's rank correlation ξ measures how nearly one continuous variable is a function of another (0 under independence, 1 for an exact functional relationship of any shape). Spearman's footrule ψ measures how close the two sets of ranks are (1 for identical rankings, 0 under independence, down to −1/2). The exact region of the pair, the set of values (ξ, ψ) that can occur together, gives every sharp inequality between the two coefficients.

What was known. Rockel (J. Comput. Appl. Math. 485, 117466, 2026) determined the region except its curved lower edge: the upper edge ψ = √ξ, the corner at footrule −1/2 (least ξ = 1/2, attained only by a checkerboard copula), the region for stochastically increasing copulas, and |ψ| ≤ √ξ for every copula. For a footrule strictly between −1/2 and 0 the least possible ξ was open; he gave a lower bound and a numerically close two-parameter family.

Results. For every footrule strictly between −1/2 and 0 the least value of ξ is attained by exactly one copula, constructed explicitly: given independent uniforms U and T, the response takes one of two levels according to whether U lies below a threshold rk(T), and the threshold solves a linear integral equation with a triangular kernel. A dual (supporting-line) inequality proves optimality over all copulas, and a quadratic stability estimate shows that nearly optimal copulas are close to the extremiser. The boundary has an elementary closed form for ψ ≤ −0.4565…, a finite piecewise-elementary evaluation elsewhere, and explicit expansions at both ends; for example ξ + 2ψ ≥ −0.6042071… for every copula. This completes the attainable region, and every attainable pair has a radially symmetric representative. Under positive or negative quadrant dependence the full regions are determined: at zero footrule the attainable values of ξ are [0, 1/2) and [0, 3/4) respectively, and neither supremum is attained. For stochastically decreasing copulas the lower edge is the same curve, ψ = 0 forces independence, and every pair with ξ ≤ −2ψ above the curve is attained; that ξ ≤ −2ψ is the exact upper edge is stated as a conjecture, supported by numerical search, not proved. The construction extends to transport problems with nonuniform margins and several displacement terms.

Limits. Population coefficients of continuous variables only, not sample estimates. Closed form only for ψ ≤ −0.4565…; elsewhere the table values are double-precision computations cross-checked by independent methods, not interval-certified. Rockel's earlier family was already numerically close (−0.193 against the exact −0.1932281… for ξ + ψ); the advance is the exact value, the proof of optimality, the unique extremiser and stability.

Contents. The paper (LaTeX source and PDF, with figure), Python scripts (NumPy, SciPy; Matplotlib for the figure) that evaluate the boundary three ways, minimise the objective independently over checkerboard copulas, check the two-predictor extension, compute the table and probe the stochastically decreasing conjecture, with their recorded outputs; plus the bibliography, a machine-readable index, a research-gate record, a review summary, a replay receipt and SHA-256 sums. Every check raises an error on failure, also under python -O.

Assurance. Written proofs; the computations test formulae and implementation and are not part of any proof. Internal AI-assisted review only: a combined five-role Claude review panel, one revision round with a bounded extension, a verification re-review, a proof audit of the new and rewritten proofs, and clean replays with a negative control. No Astra/Codex review took place. This is not peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification. Creator: Anonymous. Text CC0-1.0; code MIT.
